agent_note: The stage agent named by SARVAM_AGENT_ID in .env (Tiffany Designs Customer Service Stage). The earlier agent Tiffany-Des-0db8e21d-e099 still exists, with its own older tools calling https://tiffany-designs-customer-service.onrender.com/.
draft_note: Version 27 (committed 2026-11-11) is version 26 with the parts and open request changes, and needs the server of the same change deployed first: get_product_guide takes item (one sticker number, hardware letter, step, box, hardware or a part name such as cam bolt) and answers with just that, so on a long call the agent looks a detail up again instead of giving it from memory (the full guide drops out of view and the agent made letters and counts up); the prompt never lets it give a part, letter or count from memory, goes through a delivery check box by box, says counts as one number (अड़सठ for 68) and no longer has the cam bolts, letter A example; book_installation and register_service_request lose new_request and answer updated: a request of the same kind as one open on the order is added to that one (a reschedule moves it), and a new one is registered only when none of that kind is open. Version 26 (committed 2026-11-11) is version 23 with the context and token fixes: every tool description and input shortened (about 41,900 to 23,600 characters the model reads), because with token_based_truncation a long tool answer pushed the customer's words out and the agent replied with its greeting, and long calls lost the name and the order; the prompt keeps everything learned in the call (name, order, numbers, address, slot) and never asks for it again, answers product questions from get_product_guide, never invents counts, and never repeats the opening line; place_order no longer requires customer_name; find_order shows customer_name; temperature 0.5. Version 25 is version 24 (the same as 23) frozen; version 24 was committed from the dashboard and the phone deployment points at it. Version 23 (committed 2026-11-11) is version 22 with the order search and request details change, and needs the server of the same change deployed first: find_order without an order reference finds the orders on the number on every customer record the number is on (one is answered in full, several are named to choose from), narrowed by customer_name (in English letters, with customer_name_local in Hindi script, on find_order, find_customer and check_request_status), and finds them by customer_name with postal_code for a caller whose number is not on the order (named only, until a number confirms one); check_request_status tells what each request noted (the issue, the part and quantity, the order and product, the slot asked for) and gives the latest requests when none is open; after an invoice upload, find_order gets the WhatsApp number as order_phone. Version 22 (committed 2026-11-11) is version 21 with the caller number fix, and needs the server of the same change deployed first: find_customer, find_order, get_details_on_file, check_request_status and get_service_history are called with phone left empty for the number of this call, which the server takes from caller_phone (customer_phone); find_customer, check_request_status and get_service_history send caller_phone for the first time; a phone the model passes no longer confirms an order (only caller_phone and order_phone do); and the prompt has the agent never write, guess or say the digits of the number of this call. Version 21 (committed 2026-11-11) is version 20 with automatic language detection on for Hindi and English. Earlier: Draft 19 (2026-10-30, not committed) has every tool below as written here and the prompt in agent-prompt.md: book_installation, register_service_request, request_human_callback, place_order and save_customer_details take use_calling_number (the server puts the number of the call, from caller_phone, on the record, so the model never types the caller's digits) and contact_number_ending (the last four digits the caller confirmed; the server saves nothing on any other number and answers with the number to say back), and send_invoice_upload_link takes use_calling_number; check_invoice_upload (new) tells the agent, once the caller says the invoice is uploaded, which order the upload found or added, so the request goes on in the same call; identify_caller times out after 3 seconds (was 6) and the server answers it within CALL_START_BUDGET_MS; the default opening_line is the Hindi welcome; the silence nudges wait 10, 15, 20 and 15 seconds (a minute before the call ends). Version 18 (committed 2026-10-30) is the same without those. Version 18 and draft 19: find_order gives an order's details only once a number given in the call is the mobile number the order was placed with (number_confirmed), asks for that number otherwise (order_phone), and saves it to the agent variable order_phone; get_details_on_file, get_installation_address and the three request tools send order_phone and caller_phone (from customer_phone), and the server registers installation, damage and replacement requests only for a confirmed order. The invoice upload takes only invoices sold by Tiffany Designs Private Limited and adds the order from the invoice when none matches. Version 17 added order_number to the request tools; versions 14 to 16 had earlier copies of them. identify_caller runs at call start (lifecycle on_start) and saves customer_phone, customer_name, opening_line and caller_details. The live phone deployment answers with the version it names.
base_url_note: The server is deployed on Render. Every tool calls current_base_url + path with POST and a JSON body; change all of them together if the server moves.
response_note: Every tool answers HTTP 200 with a flat JSON object, refusals and failures included. What the agent hears is resp_template (Send fields from the API response to the agent): the message, then a Fields line with the fields in send_to_agent, for example Fields: found=True, order_id=TD-ORD-1001, open_requests=['installation']. A field the answer lacks renders empty, and error appears only when the service system did not answer. on_failure is what the agent hears when the call itself fails (timeout or a non-200). save_to_variables maps agent variables to response fields; the call-end webhook reads case_number and placed_order_number.

common_response_fields.message: What to tell the customer, plus instructions for the agent such as what to ask next. Never read out word for word.
common_response_fields.error: unavailable when the service system did not answer; absent otherwise.

tools.name: identify_caller
tools.description: Runs when the call starts, before the greeting. Sends the number the customer is calling from to the service system, which puts it in customer_phone, looks it up, and fills caller_details with what is on record for it (name, recent orders, open requests, or not on record). When the number belongs to a customer it also sets customer_name to the first name and opening_line to a greeting by name. Outbound and website calls keep the values they already have.

response_fields.customer_phone: The number of the call, E.164: the website number when one was typed, else the phone caller's number; saved to customer_phone.
response_fields.customer_name: The first name of the customer the number belongs to, or the name already set; saved to customer_name.
response_fields.opening_line: The greeting by first name for a known caller, else the greeting already set; saved to opening_line.
response_fields.caller_details: What is on record for the number (name, recent orders, open requests) or that it is not on record; saved to caller_details.
response_fields.known_customer: true when the number belongs to a customer.

tools.name: find_customer
tools.description: Finds the customer by the number of this call (phone left empty), a number the customer said, or full name with PIN code. The answer has a message with the name, recent orders and open requests, and the fields found, first_name, customer_name, number_ending, latest_order_id and open_requests. When nothing is found, carry on without saying so.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: A 10 digit number the customer said that is not the number of this call. Empty for the number of this call. Never digits the customer did not say.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: Full name in English letters, for a search without the mobile number.

parameters.name: customer_name_local
parameters.description: The same name in Hindi script, whenever customer_name is given.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: Six digit PIN code of the customer's address, with the name.

response_fields.found: true when exactly one customer matches.
response_fields.number_ending: The last four digits of the number looked up, or null for a search by name and PIN code.
response_fields.first_name: First name to address the customer by.
response_fields.recent_orders: Recent order ids with their delivery status.
response_fields.latest_order_id: The newest order id, or null.
response_fields.open_requests: How many service requests are open.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, first_name={{ first_name | default('') }}, customer_name={{ customer_name | default('') }}, number_ending={{ number_ending | default('') }}, latest_order_id={{ latest_order_id | default('') }}, open_requests={{ open_requests | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The customer lookup did not answer. Call tool:find_customer once more. When it fails again, carry on without the customer record and without saying so, and ask for the order id, order number or invoice number when the concern needs an order.

tools.name: find_order
tools.description: Finds the customer's order by order id (for example TD-ORD-1001, or the number at its end), order number of digits, invoice number, the mobile number, or full name with PIN code; call it as soon as the customer gives one. Details are given only when number_confirmed is true (the number of this call, or order_phone, is on the order); when an order matches but is not confirmed, ask which number it was placed with and call again with order_phone. Without a reference it gives the orders on the number: several_orders true means ask which one. Fields: found, number_confirmed, customer_name, several_orders, order_id, order_number, delivery_status, products, open_requests, mobile_on_order, address_on_order, details_missing. When nothing is found after a second try, or details_missing is true, offer tool:send_invoice_upload_link.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Order id as said, without spaces, for example TD-ORD-1001.

parameters.name: order_number
parameters.description: An order number of digits only, for example 122.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: Invoice number as said, without spaces, for example INV-2001.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: A 10 digit number the customer said, only to find orders without a reference. Empty for the number of this call, which the service system fills in. Never digits the customer did not say.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: Full name the order is under, in English letters, for example Meera Iyer, when the customer gives it.

parameters.name: customer_name_local
parameters.description: The same name in Hindi script, whenever customer_name is given.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: Six digit PIN code of the delivery address, with customer_name, when the reference and number find nothing.

parameters.name: order_phone
parameters.description: The 10 digit number the customer says the order was placed with, only after a tool asked for it.

response_fields.number_confirmed: true when a number given (phone, order_phone or the number of the call) is a mobile on the order's customer record; only then are the order's details given.
response_fields.several_orders: True when no order reference was given and several orders were found; the message names them to choose from.
response_fields.orders: Those orders: order_id, order_number, and for a number that confirms them, products and delivery_status.
response_fields.order_phone: The number that confirmed the order, +91 form; left out when the order is not confirmed, so a number confirmed earlier in the call stays saved. Saved to the agent variable order_phone, which the other order tools send.
response_fields.order_id: The order id, or null for a phone order.
response_fields.customer_name: Account name on the order. Not sent to the agent, so a name is never confirmed from an order id.
response_fields.delivery_status: Delivered, Shipped, Processing and so on.
response_fields.delivery_date: Delivery date as YYYY-MM-DD; the message says it as weekday and date.
response_fields.open_requests: Kinds of request open on the order: installation, installation_followup, damage, replacement.
response_fields.mobile_on_order: true when the order's customer has a mobile number on record; false means the order cannot be confirmed.
response_fields.address_on_order: true when the order has a delivery address to visit: a street, and a city or PIN code.
response_fields.details_missing: true when either is missing; the agent then offers the WhatsApp invoice upload link (Phase 15).

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, number_confirmed={{ number_confirmed | default('') }}, customer_name={{ customer_name | default('') }}, several_orders={{ several_orders | default('') }}, order_id={{ order_id | default('') }}, order_number={{ order_number | default('') }}, delivery_status={{ delivery_status | default('') }}, products={{ products | default('') }}, open_requests={{ open_requests | default('') }}{% if details_missing is defined %}, mobile_on_order={{ mobile_on_order }}, address_on_order={{ address_on_order }}, details_missing={{ details_missing }}{% endif %}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The order lookup did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:find_order once more. When it fails again, note the order id as the customer gave it and carry on without the order.

tools.name: get_details_on_file
tools.description: Gets the mobile number ending and the city, state and PIN code on file for a confirmed order or the customer, to confirm with the customer instead of asking again; the request tools fill in the rest with use_details_on_file. Call it before registering a request once the order is found, without asking first. Fields: found, mobile_on_file, mobile_ending, address_on_file, city, postal_code.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Order id that found the order, when known.

parameters.name: order_number
parameters.description: Order number that found the order, when known.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: Invoice number that found the order, when known.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: A 10 digit number the customer said, only when no order is known. Empty for the number of this call. Never digits the customer did not say.

response_fields.found: true when an order or customer was found.
response_fields.mobile_on_file: true when a mobile number is on file.
response_fields.mobile_ending: Last four digits of that mobile.
response_fields.address_on_file: true when a city or PIN code is on file.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, mobile_on_file={{ mobile_on_file | default('') }}, mobile_ending={{ mobile_ending | default('') }}, address_on_file={{ address_on_file | default('') }}, city={{ city | default('') }}, postal_code={{ postal_code | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The details on file did not answer. Ask the customer for the 10 digit mobile number, then the house, street and area, the city and the six digit PIN code, one at a time.

tools.name: get_installation_address
tools.description: For an installation on a confirmed order, gives the city, state and PIN code of the delivery address (or the customer's address on file) and the mobile number ending on file. Call it once the order is found, then ask whether to install there; when the customer agrees, book_installation is called with at_delivery_address set to true. Fields: found, address_source, city, postal_code, mobile_on_file, mobile_ending.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Order id that found the order, when known.

parameters.name: order_number
parameters.description: Order number that found the order, when known.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: Invoice number that found the order, when known.

response_fields.found: true when the order was found.
response_fields.delivered: true when the order is delivered.
response_fields.address_source: delivery, customer, or null when no address is on record.
response_fields.mobile_on_file: true when a mobile number is on file.
response_fields.mobile_ending: Last four digits of that mobile.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, address_source={{ address_source | default('') }}, city={{ city | default('') }}, postal_code={{ postal_code | default('') }}, mobile_on_file={{ mobile_on_file | default('') }}, mobile_ending={{ mobile_ending | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The installation address did not answer. Ask where the installation should be: the house, street and area, then the city, then the six digit PIN code, one at a time.

tools.name: send_invoice_upload_link
tools.description: Sends a WhatsApp link to upload a photo, screenshot or PDF of the Tiffany Designs invoice, when no order can be found or find_order says the order has no mobile number or delivery address. The invoice completes the order or adds it. Call it only after the customer agreed and the WhatsApp number was confirmed; at most 3 links per number a day. Once the customer says it is uploaded, call tool:check_invoice_upload . The answer has a message and the field sent.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The 10 digit WhatsApp number the customer said and confirmed; empty with use_calling_number.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: The customer's name, when known.

parameters.name: order_reference
parameters.description: The order id, order number or invoice number given on this call, without spaces.

parameters.name: use_calling_number
parameters.description: True when the WhatsApp number is the number of this call; phone is then left empty and the service system fills it in.

response_fields.sent: true when the link was sent.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: sent={{ sent | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The WhatsApp link could not be sent right now. Register no installation, damage or replacement request without the order: offer a call back from the service team instead, with the order id, invoice number and product the customer gave in the reason.

tools.name: check_invoice_upload
tools.description: Once the customer says the invoice is uploaded on the WhatsApp link, on this call or on a later call, says what became of it: the order the invoice found or added, with its order id or order number to look up with tool:find_order before carrying on with the concern; that no invoice has come in yet; why the invoice was not accepted; or the request the service team has it on. Call it with the WhatsApp number the link was sent to, without asking anything first. The answer has a message saying what to do next, and the fields uploaded, accepted, order_found, order_added, order_id, order_number and spoken_case_number (say it digit by digit).

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The 10 digit WhatsApp number the invoice upload link was sent to: the WhatsApp number confirmed in this call, or customer_phone on a later call unless the customer says the link came on another number.

response_fields.link_sent: false when no link was sent to these numbers in the last INVOICE_LINK_DAYS days.
response_fields.uploaded: false while no invoice has been taken on the link; null when the check could not run.
response_fields.accepted: false when the last upload was refused (the message says why); true once it went to an order or a request.
response_fields.order_found: true when the invoice was matched to an order or added as one.
response_fields.order_added: true when the order was added from the invoice (a Draft order), false when an existing order was matched.
response_fields.order_id: The order id (ERP_Order_Id__c) of that order, or null.
response_fields.order_number: The Salesforce order number of that order; find_order takes it when there is no order id.
response_fields.invoice_number: The invoice number on that order. Not sent to the agent.
response_fields.case_number: The request the invoice went to the service team on, when no order could be added. Not sent to the agent.
response_fields.spoken_case_number: That request number to say, digit by digit.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: link_sent={{ link_sent | default('') }}, uploaded={{ uploaded | default('') }}, accepted={{ accepted | default('') }}, order_found={{ order_found | default('') }}, order_added={{ order_added | default('') }}, order_id={{ order_id | default('') }}, order_number={{ order_number | default('') }}, spoken_case_number={{ spoken_case_number | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The invoice check did not answer. Apologise briefly, ask for the invoice number printed on the invoice, and call tool:find_order with it.

tools.name: get_product_guide
tools.description: Gets the product guide for an order's products or a product the customer names. With purpose parts (default): the parts by sticker number with quantity and part number, the hardware by letter with quantity, the delivery check and the product rules; use it for questions about parts and hardware and for damaged, missing or wrong parts. With purpose assembly: the complete guide with every step and its hardware, to guide self-assembly one step at a time. With item: only that part, letter, step or box, short enough to ask again whenever a detail is needed. Answer only from its message. Fields: found, has_assembly_steps, step_count; when found is false, use tool:find_parts for parts or offer an installation visit for assembly.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Order id that found the order, when known.

parameters.name: order_number
parameters.description: Order number that found the order, when known.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: Invoice number that found the order, when known.

parameters.name: product_name
parameters.description: The product named, in English, for example kitchen island, when no order is known.

parameters.name: purpose
parameters.description: parts (default) or assembly.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: Only one sticker number, hardware letter, step, box or part name, in English, for example 9, K, step 3, box 2, hardware or cam bolt.

response_fields.found: true when a published guide exists.
response_fields.purpose: parts (the default) or assembly, as the guide was asked for.
response_fields.has_assembly_steps: true when the guide has assembly steps to walk the customer through.
response_fields.products: Each product with parts_have_number_stickers and its parts (name, part_number).
response_fields.step_count: With purpose assembly, how many numbered assembly steps the guide has; 0 when it has none. Absent for parts.
response_fields.item: With item, the item looked up; the message then has only that part, letter, step or box.

tools.on_failure: The product guide did not answer. For a part, match it with tool:find_parts instead. For assembly help, offer an installation visit by the service team.

tools.name: find_parts
tools.description: Lists the parts of the products on an order, or of a product the customer names, with their part numbers. Use it when tool:get_product_guide has no guide, to match the damaged, defective, missing or wrong part and pass its part number when registering the request. The answer has a message listing each part with its part number, and the field found.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: The verified order id, for example TD-ORD-1001. Leave empty when the order is not known.

parameters.name: product_name
parameters.description: The product the customer named, for example wardrobe or study table. Used when the order id is not known.

response_fields.found: true when parts are on record.
response_fields.parts: Each part with name, part_number and product.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The part list did not answer. Record the part as the customer describes it and carry on.

tools.name: resolve_date
tools.description: Checks the installation day, and the time when one is given, using today's date and the time now in India. Installation visits are Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 6 pm, and only for a day and time still ahead; a Sunday, a time outside those hours or a time already passed is refused with what to ask instead. Call it with the day the customer said, then again with that date and the time the customer said, before reading the slot back. Never work out a date or time without it. The answer has a message to read back, and the fields valid, date (YYYY-MM-DD, for book_installation as preferred_date), spoken_date (weekday and date to say) and time (for book_installation as preferred_time).

parameters.name: date_text
parameters.description: The installation day or date the customer said, in English, for example today, tomorrow, day after tomorrow, Saturday, next Monday, 17 October or 17/10, or the YYYY-MM-DD date from an earlier resolve_date answer.

parameters.name: time_text
parameters.description: The installation time the customer said, written in English as a clock time with am or pm, for example 11 am, 3 pm, 2 pm to 4 pm or after 3 pm, or as morning, afternoon or evening when the customer gave only that. Leave empty when only the day is being checked.

response_fields.valid: true when the day, and the time when given, can be used.
response_fields.date: The date as YYYY-MM-DD, to pass to book_installation as preferred_date.
response_fields.spoken_date: The date as weekday and date, to say back.
response_fields.time: The checked time, for example 11 am or morning, 10 am to 12 pm, to pass to book_installation as preferred_time; null without time_text.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: valid={{ valid | default('') }}, date={{ date | default('') }}, spoken_date={{ spoken_date | default('') }}, time={{ time | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The date check did not answer. Ask for the day and month, then call tool:resolve_date once more. When it fails again, pass the day and the time as the customer said them to tool:book_installation, which checks them itself.

tools.name: book_installation
tools.description: Registers an installation request, or moves one (reschedule), for an order find_order found and confirmed, with the date and time from the latest resolve_date answer, after the customer confirmed the slot and the place. The slot must be Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 6 pm, and still ahead. The answer has a message with the request number and slot, or what to ask instead, and the fields created, spoken_case_number (say it digit by digit), updated (one was open on the order and is updated with this slot instead; say that request is updated) and within_business_hours.

parameters.name: preferred_date
parameters.description: Date from the latest resolve_date answer, YYYY-MM-DD.

parameters.name: preferred_time
parameters.description: Time from the latest resolve_date answer, for example 11 am or 2 pm to 4 pm.

parameters.name: reschedule
parameters.description: True to move an installation already requested.

parameters.name: existing_case_number
parameters.description: The earlier installation request number, for a reschedule, when known.

parameters.name: at_delivery_address
parameters.description: True when the customer chose the address from get_installation_address; address fields are then left empty.

parameters.name: use_details_on_file
parameters.description: True when the customer agreed to the mobile number on file; the service system fills it in.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: A 10 digit number the customer said and confirmed; empty with use_calling_number or use_details_on_file.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: Full name, first and last, of the person to contact: from caller_details, find_customer or find_order, or as the customer said it. A known name is never asked for again.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Order id that found the order, for example TD-ORD-1001; empty for a phone order.

parameters.name: order_number
parameters.description: Order number that found the order, for example 00000142; always for a phone order.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: Invoice number, when known.

parameters.name: order_source
parameters.description: Where it was bought, when the customer said so.

parameters.name: product_name
parameters.description: The product to install.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: House, street and area, only for an address other than the one on record.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: City of that address.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: Six digit PIN code of that address.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: State of that address.

parameters.name: use_calling_number
parameters.description: True when the customer wants the number of this call; phone is then left empty and the service system fills it in.

parameters.name: contact_number_ending
parameters.description: Last four digits of the mobile number, only after the customer confirmed them in this call; empty until then.

response_fields.created: true when the request is registered.
response_fields.spoken_case_number: The request number to say, digit by digit, for example 1100.
response_fields.within_business_hours: false when registered outside service hours.
response_fields.order_verified: true when the order is linked: a number given in the call (the mobile for the request, the number of the call, or order_phone) is a mobile on the order's customer record. Installation, damage and replacement requests are registered only then.
response_fields.case_id: Salesforce record id; not sent to the agent.
response_fields.contact_number_ending: The last four digits of the number the service team will call; the message says them.
response_fields.updated: true when an installation request was already open on the order: it is updated with this slot (and marked a reschedule for one), and no new request is made; case_number is that request.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: created={{ created | default('') }}, spoken_case_number={{ spoken_case_number | default('') }}, updated={{ updated | default('') }}, within_business_hours={{ within_business_hours | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The installation request could not be registered because the service system did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:book_installation once more with the same details. When it fails again, tell the customer the details are noted for the service team, who will follow up.

tools.name: register_service_request
tools.description: Registers a service request: a damaged, defective, missing or wrong part, a quality problem, a replacement, a return, an installation follow-up, a re-installation, or a general question. Except a general question, only for an order find_order found and confirmed. Call it once, after the customer confirmed the summary. The answer has a message with the request number (say it digit by digit) or what to do, and the fields created, spoken_case_number, updated (one of this kind was open on the order and is updated instead; say that request is updated) and within_business_hours.

parameters.name: issue_type
parameters.description: damaged (after delivery), delivery_damage (found on opening), defective, missing_parts, wrong_part, quality_issue, replacement, return, installation_followup, reinstallation, or general.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: The concern in one or two plain English sentences; for parts, each affected part with its part number, quantity and problem.

parameters.name: use_details_on_file
parameters.description: True when the customer agreed to the details on file; the service system fills them in.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: A 10 digit number the customer said and confirmed; empty with use_calling_number or use_details_on_file.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: Full name, first and last, of the person to contact: from caller_details, find_customer or find_order, or as the customer said it. A known name is never asked for again.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Order id that found the order, for example TD-ORD-1001; empty for a phone order.

parameters.name: order_number
parameters.description: Order number that found the order, for example 00000142; always for a phone order.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: Invoice number, when known.

parameters.name: order_source
parameters.description: Where it was bought, when the customer said so.

parameters.name: product_name
parameters.description: The product concerned.

parameters.name: part_name
parameters.description: The first affected part.

parameters.name: part_number
parameters.description: Its part number from get_product_guide or find_parts, when there is one.

parameters.name: quantity
parameters.description: How many pieces of that part are affected.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: House, street and area, only for a new address or none on file.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: City, only for a new address or none on file.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: Six digit PIN code, only for a new address or none on file.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: State, only for a new address or none on file.

parameters.name: use_calling_number
parameters.description: True when the customer wants the number of this call; phone is then left empty and the service system fills it in.

parameters.name: contact_number_ending
parameters.description: Last four digits of the mobile number, only after the customer confirmed them in this call; empty until then.

response_fields.created: true when the request is registered.
response_fields.within_business_hours: false when registered outside service hours.
response_fields.order_verified: true when the order is linked: a number given in the call (the mobile for the request, the number of the call, or order_phone) is a mobile on the order's customer record. Installation, damage and replacement requests are registered only then.
response_fields.case_id: Salesforce record id; not sent to the agent.
response_fields.contact_number_ending: The last four digits of the number the service team will call; the message says them.
response_fields.updated: true when a request of this kind was already open on the order: the details are added to it, and no new request is made; case_number is that request.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: created={{ created | default('') }}, spoken_case_number={{ spoken_case_number | default('') }}, updated={{ updated | default('') }}, within_business_hours={{ within_business_hours | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The service request could not be registered because the service system did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:register_service_request once more with the same details. When it fails again, tell the customer the details are noted for the service team, who will follow up.

tools.name: request_human_callback
tools.description: Registers a call back from the service team: when the customer asks for a person, stays upset, reports an injury or a safety risk, says a delivered order never arrived, asks to be called later, or the agent cannot help. No live transfer is available. The answer has a message with the request number (say it digit by digit) or what is missing, and the fields created, spoken_case_number and within_business_hours.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why a person should call, in one plain English sentence, with any time asked for and, when no order was found, the order id, invoice number and product given.

parameters.name: use_details_on_file
parameters.description: True when the customer agreed to the details on file; the service system fills them in.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: A 10 digit number the customer said and confirmed; empty with use_calling_number or use_details_on_file.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: Full name, first and last, of the person to contact: from caller_details, find_customer or find_order, or as the customer said it. A known name is never asked for again.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: Order id that found the order, for example TD-ORD-1001; empty for a phone order.

parameters.name: order_number
parameters.description: Order number that found the order, for example 00000142; always for a phone order.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: Invoice number, when known.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: City, only when new or none on file.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: Six digit PIN code, only when new or none on file.

parameters.name: use_calling_number
parameters.description: True when the customer wants the number of this call; phone is then left empty and the service system fills it in.

parameters.name: contact_number_ending
parameters.description: Last four digits of the mobile number, only after the customer confirmed them in this call; empty until then.

response_fields.created: true when the call back is registered.
response_fields.within_business_hours: false when registered outside service hours.
response_fields.order_verified: true when the order is linked: a number given in the call (the mobile for the request, the number of the call, or order_phone) is a mobile on the order's customer record. Installation, damage and replacement requests are registered only then.
response_fields.contact_number_ending: The last four digits of the number the service team will call; the message says them.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: created={{ created | default('') }}, spoken_case_number={{ spoken_case_number | default('') }}, within_business_hours={{ within_business_hours | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The call back request could not be registered because the service system did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:request_human_callback once more with the same details. When it fails again, tell the customer the details are noted for the service team, who will call back during service hours.

tools.name: check_request_status
tools.description: Says what the customer's requests noted and how far they have got: kind, date, order, product, the issue, the part and quantity, the slot asked for, status, visit and replacement. Use it for any question about an earlier request. With phone left empty it uses the number of this call; without a number it needs the request number with the full name or the order id. Fields: found, case_number, status, open_requests.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: A 10 digit number the customer said that is not the number of this call. Empty for the number of this call. Never digits the customer did not say.

parameters.name: case_number
parameters.description: The request number the customer gave, digits only.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: Full name in English letters, with the request number when no mobile number is known.

parameters.name: customer_name_local
parameters.description: The same name in Hindi script, whenever customer_name is given.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: The order id or number the request is about, with the request number when no mobile number is known.

response_fields.found: true when a matching request was found.
response_fields.case_number: Salesforce number of the newest request; the message has it as spoken.
response_fields.open_requests: How many requests the answer covers.
response_fields.requests: Each request: case_number, service_type, sub_type, status, closed, registered_on, order_id, order_number, issue, part and quantity.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, case_number={{ case_number | default('') }}, status={{ status | default('') }}, open_requests={{ open_requests | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The request status did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:check_request_status once more. When it fails again, offer a call back from the service team.

tools.name: get_service_history
tools.description: Lists the customer's latest service requests, closed ones included, and their latest calls with Tiffany Designs, by the number of this call, filled in by the service system, or by a mobile number the customer said. Use it when the customer asks about earlier calls or past requests. The answer has a message with the history, most recent first, and the fields found and open_requests (how many are still open).

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: A 10 digit mobile number the customer said in this call that is not the number they are calling from. Leave empty for the number of this call, which the service system fills in. Never write digits the customer did not say in this call.

response_fields.found: true when any request or call is on record.
response_fields.open_requests: How many of those requests are still open.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, open_requests={{ open_requests | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The service history did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:get_service_history once more. When it fails again, offer a call back from the service team.

tools.name: check_service_hours
tools.description: Says whether the Tiffany Designs service team is working right now and until when, or when it opens again, from the service hours and holidays in Salesforce, with the weekly hours. Use it when the customer asks about timings or wants to speak to a person, and before saying when the team will call back. The answer has a message to give, and the fields open (true when the team is working now) and hours (the weekly hours in words).

response_fields.open: true when the team is working now.
response_fields.closes_at: When it closes today, as a timestamp.
response_fields.next_open: When it opens again, as a timestamp.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: open={{ open | default('') }}, hours={{ hours | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The service hours did not answer. Say the service team works Monday to Saturday, 9 am to 6 pm, and carry on.

tools.name: check_service_area
tools.description: Says who handles service visits at a location: the Tiffany Designs service team in Delhi NCR, or an authorised service partner elsewhere, by the same rules Salesforce routes requests with. Also checks that the PIN code is valid. Use it after settling the city and PIN code for a request that needs a visit. The answer has a message to give, and the fields valid (false when the PIN code is not valid) and route (Internal or External Provider).

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: The city the customer gave, for example Gurugram or Jaipur. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: The six digit PIN code the customer gave, digits only. Leave empty when not known.

response_fields.valid: false when the PIN code is not valid or nothing was given.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: valid={{ valid | default('') }}, route={{ route | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The service area check did not answer. Carry on without it; the service system routes the request from the city and PIN code.

tools.name: find_products
tools.description: Searches the Tiffany Designs product catalogue. Use it when the customer wants to buy something or asks what a product costs, and to get the product codes place_order needs. An empty query lists everything. Only products it returns may be named. The answer has a message with each product's name, product code (for place_order, never read out) and list price in rupees, and the field found.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The product the customer described, in English, for example study table, wardrobe or kids bed. Leave empty to list every product.

response_fields.products: Each product with name, product_code (for place_order, never read out) and price in rupees.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The product list did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:find_products once more. When it fails again, say the product list is not available right now and offer a call back from the sales team.

tools.name: place_order
tools.description: Saves a new order for the sales team, who call to confirm the final price, delivery and payment; no payment is taken. Call it after the customer confirmed the products, quantities, mobile number and delivery address. The answer has a message with the order number (say it digit by digit) and total list price, or what is missing, and the fields created, spoken_order_number and total.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: Full name, first and last: from caller_details or find_customer, or as a new customer said it. A known name is never asked for again.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: A 10 digit number the customer said and confirmed; empty with use_calling_number.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: Each confirmed product as product code x quantity, separated by commas, with codes from find_products, for example TD-STD-01 x 1, TD-CHR-01 x 2.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: House or flat number, street and area.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: City.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Indian state, for example Haryana.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: Six digit PIN code.

parameters.name: notes
parameters.description: Anything else for the sales team, such as a preferred delivery time, in one short English sentence.

parameters.name: use_calling_number
parameters.description: True when the customer wants the number of this call; phone is then left empty and the service system fills it in.

parameters.name: contact_number_ending
parameters.description: Last four digits of the mobile number, only after the customer confirmed them in this call; empty until then.

response_fields.created: true when the order is saved.
response_fields.order_id: Salesforce record id; not sent to the agent.
response_fields.spoken_order_number: The order number to say, digit by digit.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: created={{ created | default('') }}, spoken_order_number={{ spoken_order_number | default('') }}, total={{ total | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The order could not be saved because the service system did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:place_order once more with the same details. When it fails again, call tool:request_human_callback with the confirmed products, their quantities and the delivery city.

tools.name: save_customer_details
tools.description: Saves a new customer's details: name, mobile number, email, another phone number and address. For a customer already on record nothing is overwritten; the details go to the service team to check first. Call it after the customer confirmed the details. The answer has a message saying what happened, or what is missing, and the fields saved and new_customer.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: A 10 digit number the customer said and confirmed; empty with use_calling_number.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: Full name, first and last; needed for a new customer.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Email address without spaces, when given.

parameters.name: alternate_phone
parameters.description: Another 10 digit phone number, when given.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: House or flat number, street and area, when given.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: City, when given.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Indian state, when given.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: Six digit PIN code, when given.

parameters.name: use_calling_number
parameters.description: True when the customer wants the number of this call; phone is then left empty and the service system fills it in.

parameters.name: contact_number_ending
parameters.description: Last four digits of the mobile number, only after the customer confirmed them in this call; empty until then.

response_fields.new_customer: true when a new customer was created; false when the change went to the team to check.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: saved={{ saved | default('') }}, new_customer={{ new_customer | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The details could not be saved because the service system did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:save_customer_details once more. When it fails again, tell the customer the details are noted for the service team, who will update them.

ids_note: Each version holds its own copy of the tools; id is the copy in version 26. Committing a draft keeps its ids for that version and opens a new draft with new ones; read them with agents get include tools before editing.
agent_variables_note: order_phone (string, empty at call start): the number that confirmed an order in find_order, saved from its answer and sent by the order tools as order_phone. caller_phone is not a variable: the tools send customer_phone under that name.
